title: BTrDB: Optimizing Storage System Design for Timeseries Processing
motivating_pain: High-rate precision time-series ingestion, versioned queries, and derived streams stress general databases.
central_principle: A version-annotated copy-on-write tree and immutable roots make time partitions and statistical aggregates version-addressable.
correctness_or_performance_argument: A root denotes one version; changed-range queries expose version deltas, while a staged implementation separates tree construction from storage.
practice_link: Year-long quasi-production deployment and multi-node Ceph-backed measurements.
evaluation_breadth: Insertion, range queries, compression, scale-out, and deployment statistics over large telemetry.
artifact_strength: Implementation and deployment evidence in the paper; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Telemetry pain -> versioned tree abstraction -> storage architecture -> implementation -> scale and deployment.
section_structure: Eight main sections, with design before quasi-production implementation and evaluation.
figure_table_role: Tree layouts and version links explain the mechanism; throughput, latency, and deployment tables carry scale evidence.
likely_reviewer_attack: External root-map/storage assumptions, retained-version reclamation, and telemetry-specific workload generality.
comparison_to_current_work: Already combines root publication, immutable history, and changed-range discovery; FrontierStore cannot claim those ideas as a new logical publication mechanism.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Recon: Verifying File System Consistency at Runtime
motivating_pain: File-system bugs can commit structurally inconsistent metadata despite crash-consistent journaling.
central_principle: Interpret block changes semantically and check offline-checker-derived invariants at each transaction boundary.
correctness_or_performance_argument: A semantic cache relates modified blocks to file-system objects; pre-commit checks cover selected invariant directions and reject corrupting transactions.
practice_link: Implemented for ext3 and Btrfs-style metadata paths and evaluated with injected corruptions and workload overhead.
evaluation_breadth: Correctness cases, corruption detection, cache behavior, and filesystem microbenchmarks.
artifact_strength: Detailed prototype and evaluation; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Production corruption examples -> semantic checking gap -> Recon design -> invariant construction -> prototype -> faults and overhead.
section_structure: Motivation and model lead directly to architecture, implementation, evaluation, limitations, and related work.
figure_table_role: Transaction dataflow diagrams establish the checking boundary; fault/overhead tables support efficacy and cost.
likely_reviewer_attack: Coverage depends on semantic interpretation and selected invariants; trusted cache/parsers may themselves fail.
comparison_to_current_work: Recon already makes an inverse/semantic relation part of commit correctness; a FrontierStore checker is differentiated only by its exact object model and independent export boundary.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: High-Performance Metadata Integrity Protection in the WAFL Copy-on-Write File System
motivating_pain: Memory scribbles and logic bugs can corrupt metadata even in a copy-on-write production file system.
central_principle: Combine incremental checksums with transaction auditing and compact consistency digests at WAFL consistency points.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Local and global relationships are summarized by digest equations; audits are aligned with copy-on-write transaction publication.
practice_link: Production-system design informed by NetApp deployment experience and long-running reliability requirements.
evaluation_breadth: Fault coverage, digest behavior, CPU and I/O overhead, consistency-point latency, and deployment-oriented cases.
artifact_strength: Production-derived implementation evidence; no public artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Threats to production metadata -> audit cost problem -> digest design -> integration -> protection and overhead -> limitations.
section_structure: Background/threats precede protection mechanisms, implementation, evaluation, experience, and related work.
figure_table_role: Metadata relationship figures explain digest scope; overhead and corruption tables quantify deployment tradeoffs.
likely_reviewer_attack: Hook completeness, probabilistic digest boundaries, proprietary implementation details, and hard-to-reproduce fleet evidence.
comparison_to_current_work: WAFL establishes that independent metadata auditing has material cost; FrontierStore must compare the full audit interface, not only its update path.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Isotope: Transactional Isolation for Block Storage
motivating_pain: Higher layers need atomic, isolated changes across block abstractions, but storage stacks expose weaker interfaces.
central_principle: Provide block-level transactions, multi-version snapshots, and isolation beneath multiple storage abstractions.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Transaction identifiers and retained versions yield atomic visibility and snapshot isolation; reclamation waits for snapshot safety.
practice_link: Prototype supports key-value and filesystem clients over multiple storage devices.
evaluation_breadth: Transaction overhead, concurrency, multiple applications, device configurations, and recovery-oriented tests.
artifact_strength: Prototype and source-level design evidence; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Cross-layer atomicity gap -> transactional block interface -> concurrency/recovery design -> prototypes -> performance.
section_structure: Motivation/model -> transaction architecture -> implementation -> evaluation -> limitations/related work.
figure_table_role: Version/transaction diagrams explain visibility; workload graphs expose isolation overhead and scaling.
likely_reviewer_attack: Hardware durability premises, snapshot garbage collection, and whether block transactions justify stack complexity.
comparison_to_current_work: Isotope shows that a common commit decision need not be a custom audit store; current-acquisition freshness is a client contract layered over transactional visibility.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Consistency Without Ordering
motivating_pain: Persistence ordering imposed for crash consistency can serialize storage and reduce performance.
central_principle: Encode logical relationships through backpointers and reconstructable metadata rather than enforce every write order.
correctness_or_performance_argument: NoFS recovers a structurally consistent namespace from unordered writes under its model and validates recovery with crash testing.
practice_link: Linux filesystem prototype and application/filebench-style workloads.
evaluation_breadth: Microbenchmarks, applications, ordering elimination, recovery scans, and crash cases.
artifact_strength: Kernel prototype and detailed measurements; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Ordering cost -> consistency-without-ordering principle -> NoFS design/recovery -> implementation -> crashes/performance.
section_structure: Problem and consistency model precede design, implementation, evaluation, and limitations.
figure_table_role: Dependency/backpointer diagrams distinguish consistency semantics; performance graphs show recovered ordering freedom.
likely_reviewer_attack: Structural consistency is weaker than transactional old-or-new data semantics; recovery scan and backpointer costs may dominate.
comparison_to_current_work: Dependency closure can likewise be weaker than complete endpoint equality; the paper motivates stating the exact observation oracle rather than equating closure with atomicity.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Application Crash Consistency and Performance with CCFS
motivating_pain: Global filesystem ordering makes application crash-consistency protocols costly and still easy to misuse.
central_principle: Separate per-application persistence streams so required orders are preserved without unnecessary cross-application ordering.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Stream order constrains crash states; application-level crash tests validate protocol outcomes under named failures.
practice_link: Linux implementation with databases, version-control, mail, and benchmark workloads.
evaluation_breadth: Application crash tests, fsync behavior, stream interactions, throughput, and latency.
artifact_strength: Kernel/application modifications and repeatable workload descriptions; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Application failures -> global-order cause -> stream interface -> filesystem design -> correctness tests -> performance.
section_structure: Empirical motivation leads to interface/mechanism, implementation, applications, evaluation, and discussion.
figure_table_role: Ordering diagrams communicate allowed crash states; application and throughput tables quantify benefit and obligations.
likely_reviewer_attack: Applications must assign streams correctly; kernel/API changes and unmodeled dependencies can invalidate guarantees.
comparison_to_current_work: CCFS reinforces that ordering is not itself a transaction theorem; FrontierStore must distinguish process-exit tests from power-loss durability and application protocol errors.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Optimizing Every Operation in a Write-Optimized File System
motivating_pain: Write-optimized trees improve inserts but naïve filesystem integration makes metadata and namespace operations slow.
central_principle: Use a B-epsilon tree across the filesystem and redesign lookup, rename, traversal, and journaling around write optimization.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Late-binding journal/checkpoint rules preserve namespace operations while batching writes through the tree.
practice_link: Linux filesystem implementation compared with mature filesystems over microbenchmarks and applications.
evaluation_breadth: Metadata operations, applications, scans, random/sequential I/O, aging, and configuration sensitivity.
artifact_strength: Substantial kernel prototype and broad evaluation; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Incomplete benefit of prior design -> operation-by-operation redesign -> implementation -> comprehensive workloads -> limits.
section_structure: Motivation and data structure lead to operation designs, implementation, evaluation, related work.
figure_table_role: Tree/operation diagrams explain algorithms; broad benchmark panels establish no single-operation cherry-pick.
likely_reviewer_attack: Kernel maturity, workload sensitivity, semantic corner cases, and whether batching shifts costs to reads/recovery.
comparison_to_current_work: A lower write count is insufficient without end-to-end audit/open/recovery cost; FrontierStore exhibits exactly this write-versus-audit tradeoff.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: F2FS: A New File System for Flash Storage
award_or_visibility_basis: High-visibility systems calibration based on mainline/mobile deployment and sustained design impact; no award claim.
motivating_pain: Traditional log-structured filesystems do not match flash translation layers, device geometry, and cleaning behavior.
central_principle: Multi-head logging, hot/cold segregation, node-address translation, and adaptive logging align placement and cleaning with flash.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Checkpoint/recovery structures preserve filesystem state; adaptive normal/threaded logging controls cleaning and write amplification.
practice_link: Linux implementation used on mobile devices and tested on multiple SSD/eMMC settings.
evaluation_breadth: Mobile applications, server workloads, utilization/aging, cleaning, write amplification, and device diversity.
artifact_strength: Deployed open-source implementation and extensive measurements; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Flash mismatch -> design principles -> on-disk structures/cleaning -> implementation -> mobile/server/aging evidence.
section_structure: Background and design precede implementation, multi-part evaluation, and related work.
figure_table_role: On-disk layout figures explain placement; sustained aging and write-amplification plots test the core mechanism.
likely_reviewer_attack: FTL opacity, device dependence, cleaning tail behavior, and benchmark/configuration tuning.
comparison_to_current_work: Selected-root compactness does not imply bounded retained space or sustained cleaning efficiency; current work must measure complete retained images and audit costs.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Fast, Transparent Filesystem Microkernel Recovery with Ananke
motivating_pain: Filesystem component crashes can require reboot or lose service even when persistent data remain recoverable.
central_principle: Log replayable operations and isolate restartable micro-components so recovery is transparent to applications.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Persistent logs plus memory checks make component restart and replay bounded under the declared p-crash model.
practice_link: User-space filesystem prototype evaluated with LevelDB/YCSB and filesystem workloads.
evaluation_breadth: Injected component failures, recovery latency, common-path overhead, memory/log costs, and applications.
artifact_strength: Substantial implementation and fault campaign; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Availability failure -> p-crash model -> logging/restart design -> implementation -> failures, overhead, and memory.
section_structure: Problem/model -> architecture/recovery -> implementation -> correctness cases -> broad evaluation -> limits.
figure_table_role: Recovery-path diagrams define the fault boundary; latency/throughput/memory plots quantify transparency cost.
likely_reviewer_attack: Fault-model coverage, trusted base, log garbage collection, and distinction from machine/power failure.
comparison_to_current_work: The distinction between process/component termination and power loss must remain explicit; FrontierStore current evidence is bounded process-level and logical validation.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Omid, Reloaded: Scalable and Highly-Available Transaction Processing
motivating_pain: Distributed key-value stores need scalable transactions without embedding concurrency control in every data tier.
central_principle: A timestamp oracle and commit table supply snapshot-isolated transactions while preserving separation from the storage layer.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Read/write protocols consult commit metadata to expose one snapshot; high availability follows replicated transaction metadata.
practice_link: Production-oriented HBase deployment and scale experiments.
evaluation_breadth: Throughput, contention, failures, scale-out, metadata overhead, and comparison with transaction managers.
artifact_strength: Implementation and production-oriented evaluation; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Transaction-layer gap -> architecture/protocol -> safety/availability -> implementation -> throughput and failure evidence.
section_structure: Motivation and model lead to protocol, recovery/HA, implementation, evaluation, related work.
figure_table_role: Protocol timelines explain commit visibility; scale and failure graphs establish transaction-manager behavior.
likely_reviewer_attack: Snapshot-isolation anomalies, oracle/commit-table bottlenecks, and availability assumptions.
comparison_to_current_work: A common visibility frontier can be relational and replicated rather than one file; the exact relational reduction therefore defeats a logical uniqueness claim.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Holistic and Automated Task Scheduling for Distributed LSM-tree-based Storage
motivating_pain: Foreground reads and background compaction interfere across replicas, producing imbalance and tail-latency spikes.
central_principle: Jointly schedule foreground and maintenance tasks using replica state instead of optimizing each layer independently.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Scheduling objective and feedback allocate work across decoupled replicas; claims are performance rather than transactional correctness.
evaluation_breadth: YCSB mixes, skew, value size, consistency levels, saturation, throughput, tail latency, and resource use.
artifact_strength: Public artifact instructions and scripts are included; artifact not executed here.
story_sequence: Cross-layer interference -> holistic scheduler -> implementation -> extensive sensitivity and resource evaluation.
section_structure: Motivation/analysis -> design -> implementation -> twelve-plus experiments -> limitations/related work.
figure_table_role: Queue/scheduling diagrams motivate coupling; dense workload plots test breadth and tail behavior.
likely_reviewer_attack: Reliance on replica decoupling/selection, large testbed assumptions, and transfer to other engines.
comparison_to_current_work: It calibrates the need for sustained and sensitivity evidence; one favorable update microbenchmark would not establish a storage contribution.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: WiscKey: Separating Keys from Values in SSD-Conscious Storage
motivating_pain: LSM trees repeatedly rewrite large values and suffer read/write amplification on SSDs.
central_principle: Keep keys in the sorted tree and append values to a separate log, then prefetch and garbage-collect values.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Key entries point to value-log locations; append/recovery and garbage collection preserve reachability while reducing tree write volume.
practice_link: LevelDB-derived implementation on commodity SSDs using YCSB and database workloads.
evaluation_breadth: Loads, reads/writes, scans, value sizes, garbage collection, SSD characteristics, throughput, and amplification.
artifact_strength: Substantial prototype and broad reproducible methodology; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: LSM amplification -> separation principle -> consistency/GC design -> implementation -> performance and sensitivity.
section_structure: Problem analysis -> design -> implementation -> experiments -> discussion/related work.
figure_table_role: Data-path diagrams explain separation; throughput and amplification plots establish the tradeoff envelope.
likely_reviewer_attack: Garbage-collection cost, scans, small values, value-log crash handling, and SSD dependence.
comparison_to_current_work: Like WiscKey, FrontierStore lowers rewriting by changing representation; unlike WiscKey, its current full-audit latency loses to the inspected generic rooted composition.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

central_principle: Combine large fleet telemetry with controlled statistical stratification rather than infer reliability from device specifications.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Statistical models and controlled subgroup analyses separate observed associations from simple temperature folklore.
practice_link: Large production datacenter fleet and operational environmental records.
evaluation_breadth: Disk models, age, temperature, humidity, workload and datacenter slices with failure-rate analysis.
artifact_strength: Rare large-scale field dataset; raw fleet data are not reproduced in this calibration.
story_sequence: Operational question -> prior-confounding gap -> dataset/method -> multivariate results -> implications and limits.
section_structure: Motivation/related data -> methodology -> environmental analyses -> operational interpretation -> limitations.
figure_table_role: Population tables define cohorts; stratified plots make confounding and non-monotone effects visible.
likely_reviewer_attack: Observational confounding, vendor/era specificity, selection effects, and unavailable raw production data.
comparison_to_current_work: It calibrates measurement provenance: process-accounted write bytes must not be presented as physical-device traffic.

title: Noria: Dynamic, Partially-Stateful Data-Flow for High-Performance Web Applications
motivating_pain: Application caches and denormalized views require manual invalidation, over-materialization, and difficult migrations.
central_principle: Use partially materialized dataflow with upqueries so only demanded state is retained and maintained.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Dataflow update propagation plus domain-aware upqueries preserve view behavior under dynamic graph changes and races.
practice_link: Lobsters-like application and distributed implementation with realistic web workloads.
evaluation_breadth: Application conversion, reads/writes, partial materialization, memory, failures, migrations, and scale-out.
artifact_strength: Large systems prototype and application evidence; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Web-state pain -> partial-state principle -> dataflow semantics -> implementation -> application and systems evaluation.
section_structure: Motivation/model -> design/races -> implementation -> application/evaluation -> limitations/related work.
figure_table_role: Dataflow and upquery diagrams explain state flow; application/scale graphs quantify memory/performance.
likely_reviewer_attack: Eventual-view semantics, SQL/operator coverage, memory under adversarial access, and operational complexity.
comparison_to_current_work: Noria tracks computation and can recompute missing state; FrontierStore stores opaque declared dependencies and should not claim equivalent semantic incrementality.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: GoJournal: A Verified, Concurrent, Crash-Safe Journaling System
motivating_pain: Verified filesystems often sacrifice concurrency or performance because crash reasoning does not compose with shared-memory code.
central_principle: Perennial specifications, logically atomic reasoning, and crash-aware lifting verify a concurrent write-ahead journal.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Machine-checked Coq proofs connect Go implementation behavior to concurrent and crash specifications under explicit trusted assumptions.
practice_link: Integrated journal evaluated through an NFS server against Linux implementations.
evaluation_breadth: Proof size, concurrency, NFS workloads, crashes, microbenchmarks, and performance stability.
artifact_strength: Artifact appendix includes proof checking and performance scripts; not executed in this calibration.
story_sequence: Verification/concurrency gap -> logic and journal design -> machine proof -> implementation -> NFS performance -> trusted base.
section_structure: Specification/logic -> design -> verification -> implementation -> evaluation -> related work/artifact.
figure_table_role: Protocol/proof diagrams expose refinement boundaries; code-size and performance graphs quantify practicality.
likely_reviewer_attack: Trusted stack and hardware model, locking premise, proof engineering cost, and environment-sensitive performance.
comparison_to_current_work: Bounded tests and hand arguments do not approach implementation refinement; the final paper must state its result as finite evidence rather than verified crash safety.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Storage Systems Are Distributed Systems (So Verify Them That Way!)
motivating_pain: Storage software interacts asynchronously with devices and crashes, defeating sequential verification models.
central_principle: Model the storage device as a distributed asynchronous environment and connect protocol proofs to code proofs.
correctness_or_performance_argument: TLA+-style protocol invariants and Dafny/Hoare reasoning establish crash-safe linearizable behavior for VeriBetrKV.
practice_link: Verified key-value store with measured performance against RocksDB and verification-engineering accounting.
evaluation_breadth: Correctness proof corpus, crash behavior, workload performance, scaling, and proof/code effort.
artifact_strength: Machine-checked specifications and implementation evidence; no artifact execution in this calibration.
story_sequence: Asynchrony analogy -> protocol specification -> refinement/code verification -> storage implementation -> performance and lessons.
section_structure: Model and methodology -> protocol proof -> code proof -> system/evaluation -> lessons/related work.
figure_table_role: State-machine diagrams define asynchronous boundaries; proof-size and benchmark tables balance rigor and cost.
likely_reviewer_attack: Trusted runtime/device model, approximately order-of-magnitude performance gap, and high proof complexity.
comparison_to_current_work: It supplies the proof bar for claiming crash-safe storage; FrontierStore instead offers a finite model, executable checker, and explicit non-refinement boundary.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: DBSP: Automatic Incremental View Maintenance for Rich Query Languages
motivating_pain: Existing incremental view maintenance techniques are fragmented by query language and operator class.
central_principle: A stream calculus and algebraic differentiation transform rich batch queries into incremental computations.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Algebraic theorems, supported by Lean formalization, establish semantic equivalence of incrementalized operators.
practice_link: Language/compiler architecture and examples; the paper explicitly leaves full systems performance evaluation to subsequent work.
evaluation_breadth: Formal operator coverage, examples, complexity discussion, and mechanized mathematics rather than a broad performance campaign.
artifact_strength: Lean-checked mathematical development and implementation pointer; not executed in this calibration.
story_sequence: Fragmented IVM -> stream model -> derivatives/operators -> formal properties -> language coverage -> future system evaluation.
section_structure: Motivation/notation -> calculus -> operator constructions -> formalization -> related work/limitations.
figure_table_role: Algebraic tables summarize operators; examples carry semantic intuition rather than systems benchmarks.
likely_reviewer_attack: Systems practicality and end-to-end performance are deferred; assumptions for non-linear/recursive workloads.
comparison_to_current_work: DBSP provides semantic recomputation, while FrontierStore only persists declared facts; a transactional DBSP composition is a stronger null than a custom fact store alone.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.

title: Provenance Semirings
motivating_pain: Why-, where-, lineage-, multiplicity-, and probabilistic provenance had incompatible ad hoc semantics.
central_principle: Annotate relations over commutative semirings so query operators propagate a general provenance algebra.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Algebraic theorems show how homomorphisms specialize universal annotations to multiple provenance interpretations.
practice_link: Worked relational-query examples and connections to incomplete/probabilistic databases; no storage engine evaluation.
evaluation_breadth: Formal definitions, equivalence arguments, and examples rather than empirical systems evidence.
artifact_strength: Self-contained mathematical result; no executable artifact used.
story_sequence: Fragmented provenance notions -> K-relations -> positive relational algebra -> universal property -> specializations.
section_structure: Definitions and algebraic results dominate, followed by provenance interpretations and related work.
figure_table_role: Equations and examples, not performance figures, carry the contribution.
likely_reviewer_attack: No physical storage/performance design, limits around recursion/difference, and practical annotation growth.
comparison_to_current_work: A flat dependency set discards alternative derivations and multiplicity; FrontierStore is a conservative invalidation representation, not a provenance-semiring system.
inspection_scope: Complete full text and relevant displays inspected; artifact not executed.
